argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only in a caveated form. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.1 percentage points, the launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the rollout is staged with a 7% initial cohort and a rollback switch. The overbroad part is not the certification direction itself, but any reading of it as unconditional. The same admissible evidence also shows that telehealth discharge planning is below target on post-visit instruction summarization, remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort, and is not covered by an approved risk acceptance. The defensible packet is therefore certification with an explicit condition: launch requires model-card disclosure of that named limitation unless approved risk acceptance covering that use case is completed before launch.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis for the argument. On the admissible record, the correct governance posture is to avoid escalation beyond a caveat where the remaining gap can be handled by an explicit pre-launch disclosure condition or a completed approved risk acceptance.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy does not allow rollout controls alone to cure the weakness because the affected use case remains exposed. The admissible evidence supports a narrow policy-compliant interpretation: certification is supportable if and only if the audit packet binds launch to explicit disclosure of the telehealth discharge planning limitation, unless an approved risk acceptance specifically covering that exposure is completed before launch. Public governance guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring deployment risk supports that conditional posture, but does not replace the disclosure predicate in the policy text.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence of an approved risk acceptance that specifically names telehealth discharge planning exposure.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has already been completed or attached.
The current record directly supports a staged rollout and rollback switch, but not a broader claim of fully evidenced monitoring controls.
An unqualified certify_model action would overstate what the admissible evidence supports.
